newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lebanese demonstrate in Paris against Syria.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese demonstrate in Paris against Syria.

text.p: Several dozen Lebanese nationalists have demonstrated outside Syria's embassy in Paris, asking French President Jacques Chirac to seek the release of Lebanese prisoners held in Syrian or Israeli jails, eyewitnesses said.

The demonstration, which took place late on Sunday while Chirac was on an official visit to Damascus, was called by the "Rally for Lebanon" movement which comprises mostly Lebanese Christian Maronites living in the French capital.
Eyewitnesses said riot police outnumbered participants who lit candles on the pavement outside the embassy spelling the word "Freedom." No arrests were reported.

Rally president Simon Abi Ramia told those present: "Our candles are lit so that the French president and the international community do not forget the Lebanese detained in Syria and those in Israeli jails...so they do not forget that freedom itself is a prisoner in Lebanon."
Paris hosts an array of Lebanese nationalist groups who oppose the Syrian-supported government now in power in Beirut.
